P.C. : 
The petitioner has made the following prayers in th is Writ
Petition :-
“(a) That this Hon’ble Court be pleased to issue the Rule  and
call for records and proceedings; 
 (b) This  Hon’ble  Court  be  pleased  to  issue  a  writ  of
mandamus  or  certiorari  or  any  other  appropriate,
writ/direction/order in the nature of writ of manda mus or
certiorari under Article 226 of the Constitution of India,
1950, thereby direct the respondent nos.1 and 2 to ta ke
proper  legal  action  and  take  cognizance  against  the
accused persons in accordance with law; 
 (c) Pending the hearing and final disposal of the prese nt Writ
Petition,  this  Hon’ble  Court  be  pleased  to  direct  to  th e
respondent  nos.1  and  2  to  enquire  the  matter  and  file
report before this Hon’ble Court;
 (d) Interim/ad-interim  order  in  terms  of  prayer  clause  (c)
above be granted;
 (e) Such other and further reliefs be granted as the nature
and circumstances of the case may be required.”

2. The petitioner states that she is a widow and a w orking
woman. This is the case set up by the petitioner th at a proposal
for the marriage of her daughter was moved by her o wn sister and
brother-in-law and “seeing ceremony” took place on 26th November
2023. In connection to the marriage negotiations, s he gave five
tolas  of  gold  for  the  bride,  two  tolas  gold  for  the  groom  and
Rs.2,50,000/- in cash as dowry. She further states t hat there was
a further demand to bear the cost of five cars but she was unable
to meet the demand and cancelled the marriage proposal.
3. In the aforesaid facts, the petitioner states tha t the accused
persons who received five tolas of gold and Rs.2,50 ,000/- cash
have now declined to return such articles to her an d, therefore,
she made a complaint to the police. The grievance of the petitioner
is that the police has yet not taken any steps in t he matter and
did not conduct investigation.
4. As stated in paragraph no.5 of this writ petition , if this is the
case  set  up  by  the  petitioner  that  she  herself  canc elled  the
marriage proposal, in our opinion, no criminality c an be attached
to the transaction which took place between the petitioner and the
accused persons. In that view of the matter, no ind ulgence can be
granted in the present writ petition and, according ly, Writ Petition
No.4929 of 2025 is dismissed.
    [ GAUTAM A. ANKHAD, J. ]       [ CHIEF JUSTICE ]
